questions.question: What is the most effective way to clear haze from the inside of the windows?
options: Switch on the air conditioning system
Wipe the glass with a dry cloth while driving
Turn the ventilation fan off completely
Switch on the hazard warning lights
questions.explanation: Air conditioning dries the air in the cabin, so the moisture condensing on the glass is removed at its source; rear window and mirror heating help as well.

questions.question: Why must you be especially careful around pedestrians and cyclists in bad weather?
options: They hear and see about as well as in good weather
They are easier to notice because of their rain gear
They hear and see worse than in good weather
They usually keep further away from the roadway
questions.explanation: Wind, rain and hoods cut down their hearing and vision, and children often shield their faces with their hands, so they may not notice an approaching car.

questions.question: Where does strong wind pose the greatest danger to a car on the road?
options: Where the wind blows steadily across a flat open plain
Where the road runs between tall buildings in a town
Where the road follows the shore of a sheltered bay
Where the wind strength varies, such as along a mountain ridge
questions.explanation: A sudden change in wind strength shoves the car sideways without warning, and the higher your speed the more violent that effect becomes.

questions.question: What is the safest thing to do when a sand storm is blowing?
options: Drive on slowly with the hazard lights switched on
Wait in shelter until the storm has passed
Drive through it as quickly as you safely can
Follow closely behind a larger vehicle for cover
questions.explanation: Blown sand can ruin the windscreen and strip the paint coating, so staying off the carriageway until it passes is better than driving through it.

questions.question: Your right-hand wheels drop off the asphalt onto the gravel shoulder. What should you do?
options: Brake hard at once and steer straight back onto the asphalt
Accelerate so the wheels climb the edge more easily
Keep your speed and turn the wheel sharply back to the left
Hold a steady course, slow down, then ease back onto the road
questions.explanation: A steep edge between asphalt and gravel grabs the tire; any sudden steering or braking at speed can flip the car back across the road out of control.

questions.question: At roughly what temperature is a road covered with ice or snow usually most slippery?
options: Around minus 10 °C
Around 0 °C
Around minus 20 °C
Below minus 25 °C
questions.explanation: Near freezing point a film of water forms on top of the ice, and hidden slippery patches build up in ruts as the temperature crosses zero.

questions.question: If your wheels spin as you try to move off on snow, what should you do?
options: Press harder on the gas until the tires bite through
Let the car roll back a little, then accelerate gently again
Hold the brake and the gas pedal down at the same time
Release the clutch quickly while revving the engine
questions.explanation: Spinning a wheel is useless and can damage the car or the tires; rolling back onto fresh ground, or laying a rug under the tire, lets it find grip.

questions.question: Which of these is listed as a common reason a car starts to slide on a slippery road?
options: Running the tires at too low a pressure
Carrying too heavy a load in the boot
Giving the car too much gas
Keeping too long a following distance
questions.explanation: Sliding comes from how the car is handled: excessive speed, too much acceleration, braking too hard, or steering more than the grip allows.

questions.question: You have to leave the car parked on a slippery slope. What is good practice?
options: Leave the car in neutral with the handbrake released
Point the front wheels straight along the slope
Wedge the front wheels against a fixed edge such as a kerb
Park with the rear wheels resting on loose snow
questions.explanation: The handbrake alone may not hold on ice, so a physical block against the wheels keeps the car from sliding away once you have left it.

questions.question: During which period is the use of studded tires prohibited?
options: 15 April to 31 October
1 April to 1 November
15 March to 30 September
1 May to 15 October
questions.explanation: Studs are only allowed through the winter season because they wear the road surface far faster than unstudded tires, unless circumstances state otherwise.

questions.question: Dust thrown up by the vehicle ahead is cutting your visibility. What should you do?
options: Increase the gap and make sure the headlights are on
Close the gap so you can keep the vehicle in sight
Switch to parking lights and hold your speed
Overtake at once to get clear of the dust
questions.explanation: More distance buys you time to see through the dust cloud, and headlights make your own car visible to anyone coming the other way.

questions.question: There are pools of water beside the pavement where pedestrians are walking. What should you do?
options: Slow down enough that the car does not splash them
Swerve out around the pools to keep clear of them
Hold your speed and steer through the middle of them
Switch on the hazard lights while you pass them
questions.explanation: Soaking pedestrians is avoidable simply by easing off; swerving is a separate hazard because another vehicle may be alongside you or in your blind spot.

questions.question: Driving at 90 km/h on a wet road gives roughly the same grip as driving on ice at what speed?
options: 30 km/h
45 km/h
60 km/h
75 km/h
questions.explanation: Grip on a wet surface falls away as speed rises, until the tires float on the water; the comparison shows how little margin is left at summer speeds.

questions.question: Your car has gone into deep water and the doors will not open. What should you do?
options: Open a window to let water in and equalise the pressure
Push the door open hard before the water rises further
Break the windscreen out before the water reaches it
Wait on the bottom and then push a door open
questions.explanation: Outside water pressure holds the doors shut until the pressure inside matches it, so letting water in through a window is what makes an exit possible.

questions.question: Why is off-road driving so damaging in the Icelandic highlands?
options: It packs the gravel so hard that plants grow back too thickly
It drives farm animals away from their grazing grounds
A wheel track lets water in and can grow into a lasting scar
It leaves oil in the soil that poisons the vegetation
questions.explanation: Vegetation gets more fragile with elevation, and a broken surface erodes in later rains, so an innocent-looking track becomes a wound that heals very slowly.

questions.question: What trailer may the holder of a category B licence tow?
options: Up to 750 kg only, whatever the weight of the towing car
Up to 1,000 kg, or heavier if the total stays within 3,500 kg
Any weight, provided the trailer has brakes of its own
Up to 750 kg, or heavier if car and trailer stay within 3,500 kg
questions.explanation: The 750 kg figure is the free allowance; above it the combined weight limit applies, and the trailer may never exceed the figure in the car's registration.

questions.question: Compared with driving in daylight, how much greater is the risk of a traffic accident in the dark?
options: About twice as great
About five times as great
About the same as in daylight
About three times as great
questions.explanation: Drivers tend not to reduce speed enough for the shorter distance the headlights actually reveal, which is what drives the risk up in darkness.

questions.question: When is it appropriate to use the main beam (high beam)?
options: In the dark on lit streets inside built-up areas
In the dark out in the country where traffic is light
In heavy rain at any time of day or night
When following close behind another vehicle
questions.explanation: Main beam reaches 100 metres or more but has no glare control, so it may only be used where there is nobody ahead to be dazzled by it.

questions.question: Where should you place your car when meeting another vehicle in the dark on a road with lane markings?
options: As close to the centre dividing line as you can
As close to the right-hand edge of the road as you can
As close to the centre of your own lane as you can
Just outside the right-hand edge line of your lane
questions.explanation: Too near the dividing line and your lights dazzle the oncoming driver; too near the edge and you risk hitting a pedestrian, cyclist or parked vehicle.
